title: Measuring Up for a New Lens

patient.name: Mdm Fatimah Binte Hassan
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for optical biometry — listed for right cataract surgery (phaco + IOL)

history.hpc: Mdm Fatimah says 'My right eye blur already, more than six months, slowly slowly, no pain one.' She was referred from a polyclinic and seen at another hospital before. The doctor has confirmed cataracts in both eyes, listed her for right eye phacoemulsification with intraocular lens, and ordered optical biometry to calculate the lens power.
history.pmhx: Bilateral cataracts. Dry eyes in both eyes. No diabetes. No previous eye surgery.
history.social_hx: Retired homemaker. Lives with family. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: nuclear sclerosis 2+ with posterior subcapsular cataract. Left eye: nuclear sclerosis 1+. Reduced tear film in both eyes
examination_findings.fundus: No retinal detachment. Cup-to-disc ratio 0.4 in both eyes

optical_biometry.signal_to_noise: Good (SNR above threshold on repeated measurements)
optical_biometry.iol_power: Calculated with an appropriate modern formula for the surgeon's target refraction; values handed to surgeon

diagnosis: Optical biometry of the right eye completed with good signal quality and consistent repeat measurements. Axial length, keratometry, anterior chamber depth and lens thickness obtained and the IOL power calculated for the surgeon's chosen lens and target refraction. The dry eye / unstable tear film was noted as it can affect keratometry, and measurements were repeated after the surface was optimised. Results provided to the surgeon for IOL selection.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm the operative eye (right) against the surgical listing
Optimise the ocular surface before keratometry (ensure a stable tear film; ask the patient to blink fully) as dry eye can distort K readings
Explain the procedure: non-contact, look at the fixation light, takes a few minutes, no eye drops or touching the eye needed
Enter patient details accurately and select the biometry program
Position the patient at the chinrest, align on the visual axis and capture axial length, keratometry, ACD, lens thickness and white-to-white
Take repeated measurements and check the signal-to-noise / consistency; repeat any reading that is inconsistent or low quality
Enter the surgeon's IOL constant and target, review the calculated IOL powers and hand the printout to the surgeon
follow_up: Surgeon to select the IOL power and lens model based on the biometry and target refraction
If measurements are unreliable (e.g. dense cataract blocking axial length), arrange immersion ultrasound A-scan as a backup
Confirm biometry is filed against the correct eye before surgery
patient_education: Explain that the measurements decide the power of the new lens that will replace the cloudy lens
Reassure the patient it is quick, painless and does not touch the eye
Advise on using her lubricating drops to keep the eye surface healthy before surgery

key_points: Confirms patient identity and verifies the correct operative eye against the listing
Notes the dry eye history as relevant to keratometry accuracy
Confirms the surgery booked and the purpose of biometry (IOL power)
Explains the non-contact procedure to the patient
Optimises the tear film before keratometry and obtains a stable surface
Aligns the patient correctly and captures axial length, K, ACD, lens thickness and white-to-white
Takes repeat measurements and checks signal quality/consistency, repeating poor readings
Enters the correct IOL constant and surgeon target before calculating
Understands that biometry provides the measurements for IOL power calculation
Recognises that dry eye and dense cataract can affect measurement quality
Does not select the IOL independently — provides results to the surgeon
Knows immersion A-scan is the backup if optical axial length cannot be obtained
Captures consistent, good-quality biometry for the correct eye
Repeats inconsistent measurements rather than accepting poor data
Hands accurate results to the surgeon and files against the correct eye
Educates the patient on the purpose of the test and ocular surface care
